nv_the_gallery.blurb: A compact sandstone sport wall in the Calico Hills of Red Rock, tucked among the Second Pullout crags. Twenty routes, nearly all bolted with a single trad line, and the spread leans hard: a couple of easy warm-ups, a handful of 5.10s, then a steady block of 5.11 through 5.13 lines that make up most of the wall. The routes are well protected and have comfortable belay spots, which is why it is a favourite for pushing grades. Parking nearby is tight, so expect to share the walk in with plenty of other climbers on good days.

nv_mossy_ledges_area.blurb: A quiet, rarely visited sandstone cliff in the Willow Spring zone of Red Rock, around the corner from the Case Face. Almost everything here is traditional, with just one bolted line, and the grades stay mostly moderate: a few easy climbs, a good run of 5.7 to 5.9, and only a couple of routes at 5.10 or 5.11. Most lines face north and stay shaded, and parts of the stone are thick with moss, so it suits warm days better than cold ones. Old bolts and pitons hint at decades of forgotten climbing. Expect solitude, scrappy sections and a short hillside scramble in.

nv_aeolian_wall.blurb: A huge diamond-shaped sandstone face that fills the right side of Mt. Wilson in Red Rock, and one of the area's big-wall objectives. Routes are long multi-pitch trad and aid lines, running from a few to over twenty pitches, with the grades clustered between 5.10 and 5.11 and a couple harder and easier outliers. Expect steep, overhanging stretches in the middle of the wall, mossy cracks, and slabbier, sparsely protected ground higher up. The approach and descent are serious undertakings through gullies and 4th-class ground, so this is for experienced parties planning a long, committing day or a bivy.

nv_the_secret_13_wall.blurb: A steep, overhanging sandstone sport wall in the Sandstone Quarry zone of Red Rock, known for the densest cluster of hard bolted routes in the park. All twenty lines are sport, and nothing here is easy: the grades start at 5.11, with the bulk at 5.12 and 5.13 and a few reaching into 5.14. Routes are short, around 60 to 70 feet, with long roofy sections broken by the occasional vertical stretch. The rock is soft, and holds can change over time. The wall is mostly in the shade and holds seepage, so it can take a while to dry out.

nb_minkey_wall.blurb: A granite trad wall high on the hillside at Cochrane Lane Cliffs near Welsford, widely regarded as the best trad wall at the crag. All 28 routes need your own gear, spanning 5.5 to 5.12 with most between 5.9 and 5.11. Lines are about 30 metres long and mostly vertical, with a few pulling through a big roof left of centre. The wall looks imposing but most climbs protect well, while a few bolder ones demand a calm head. The right side is a tangle of leaning cracks and variations, so a topo helps you sort out lines.
